subject: MSA/Order Form — SLA & support redlines, maintenance cadence and legal handoff
body:
From: Alexandra Gupta <alexandra.gupta@zephyrus.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — SLA questions and maintenance windows

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo and the draft order form. Legal at Zephyrus reviewed the SLA section and had a few specific asks before we can move to procurement:

- Can Redwood confirm a 99.95% uptime commitment for the dedicated environment (pinned model) and include the calculation window (monthly rolling)?
- Service credit formula: they want a waterfall that caps at 30% for a monthly outage > 12 hours; they prefer a per-minute calculation rather than slab bands.
- Response times: P1 acknowledged as 1-hour response; request to clarify time-to-resolution targets vs. acknowledgment.
- Maintenance windows: Zephyrus requires a 48-hour blackout for any rolling cluster upgrades that would change SLA measurements; also they asked for a max of 4 scheduled maintenance events per quarter for Dedicated pools.

I've attached our internal markups (see attached). We'd like Redwood legal to propose language for: uptime definition, exclusion carve-outs (network/provider interruptions), and a fall-back plan when a model variant needs rollback that affects KV cache and stateful sessions.

Could you route this to your contracts team? We need a redlined MSA + Order Form by next Tuesday (2027-05-18) to keep the procurement window.

Best,
Alex
Procurement Lead, Zephyrus AI

Attachments: Zephyrus_Initial_SLA_asks.pdf (summary)

------

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Alexandra Gupta <alexandra.gupta@zephyrus.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — SLA questions and maintenance windows

Alexandra,

Thanks — looping in Marissa (sales) and Aditya (legal ops) to coordinate the redline. Quick read: we can accept a 99.95% uptime target for the Dedicated offering, but we need to align on the calculation method and exclusions. A few immediate clarifications:

- Rolling monthly window is fine; our metrics are measured as "total available minutes" vs. "downtime minutes" per calendar month, and we report via the Console with audit logs available on request.
- We can support a per-minute credit calculation but have threshold minimums (we don't typically pay credits for sub-minute blips caused by carrier routing). We'll propose an agreed minimum outage bucket (30s) to avoid noise.
- For P1: our SLA language separates "Acknowledgement" (within 1 hour) and "Operational Mitigation" (initial workaround within 4 hours) with a separate TTR ladder based on severity. We will propose that structure.
- Maintenance cadence: we want to keep weekly minor patches (no SLA impact) but agree on a max of 4 scheduled disruptive maintenances per quarter for changes that materially affect availability. For emergency security patching we'll have a carve-out with prior notice where feasible.

Aditya, can you take point on drafting the redline for distribution? Marissa, FYI for the procurement timeline — Zephyrus wants the redlined doc by 2027-05-18.

Laura Bennett
Head of Contracts, Redwood Inference

------

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — SLA questions and maintenance windows

Thanks Laura — a couple of negotiation guardrails from sales perspective:

- We can accept 99.95% for Dedicated for this account, but only if Zephyrus agrees to a contractual limitation on runbook-driven retries (i.e., they must follow our recommended retry/backoff patterns for high-throughput telemetry).
- The per-minute credit is okay as long as it's bounded (cap at 30% monthly) and we keep an explicit carve-out for customer-induced outages (misconfigured endpoints, credential exposures, heavy prefix poisoning causing KV growth).
- On maintenance events, we must keep the ability to do one additional emergency maintenance per quarter without triggering credits (security/fix). We'll mark that as "emergency exception" and propose a 72-hour notice where possible.

Also, if Zephyrus insists on per-minute billing for credits, we should offer alternative mitigations: increased monitoring/tracing retention for free for the first 90 days and an onboarding run to bake in caching patterns to lower incidence. That value-add helps the deal economics.

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales — Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

------

From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: Alexandra Gupta <alexandra.gupta@zephyrus.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 14:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form — SLA & support redlines, maintenance cadence and legal handoff

Alexandra / Samuel,

Following internal review we've prepared a consolidated redline bundle attached (Zephyrus_MSA_OrderForm_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx) and a cleaned support matrix (support-coverage-matrix_v2.xlsx). Highlights of changes we propose:

1) Uptime definition and measurement
- Uptime = (Total minutes in month - Downtime minutes attributable to Redwood) / Total minutes. We propose measurement via Redwood Console telemetry with a 10-business-day dispute window after monthly reporting.

2) Credits and cap
- Per-minute credits accepted; calculation: (Downtime minutes / Total minutes) * Monthly Service Fee, capped at 30% per month. Minimum outage bucket: 30 seconds for automated noise filtering.

3) Response and TTR ladder
- Acknowledgement = 1 hour for P1; Operational Mitigation = 4 hours; Target Resolution (best-effort) tiers defined in appendix A. Credits trigger based on downtime, not time-to-resolution.

4) Maintenance and blackouts
- Scheduled disruptive maintenance limited to 4 events per rolling quarter. Non-disruptive patches (kernel, minor code updates) excluded.
- Emergency maintenance (security) permitted once per quarter without credit if Redwood provides notice within 24 hours post-action and a remediation plan.

5) Exclusions and customer responsibilities
- We added explicit language carving out outages caused by customer misconfiguration, third-party infra outages (cloud provider), and force majeure.

Next steps:
- Please review the attached redline and support matrix. If you have edits, mark changes and return by EOD 2027-05-19 so procurement can scope DocuSign and internal approvals.
- If Zephyrus wants a bridge arrangement for the 90-day onboarding window (reduced credits + onboarding run), Marissa is prepared to include the onboarding package as part of the order form.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Zephyrus_MSA_OrderForm_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (redline), support-coverage-matrix_v2.xlsx (support coverage and escalation ladder)

------

On Mon, 17 May 2027 16:45:00 +0000 Alexandra Gupta <alexandra.gupta@zephyrus.ai> wrote:

> Hi Aditya, Laura, Marissa —
>
> Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear redline bundle. We reviewed the doc and have a couple of minor asks before we finalize: 
>
> 1) Could you change the minimum outage bucket to 60 seconds rather than 30? Our monitoring registers lots of <1min blips from upstream proxies and we want to avoid frequent credit triggers.
> 2) For emergency maintenance carve-out, can we accept "notice within 48 hours" rather than 24? Our internal ops need that cushion for legal review.
>
> We'll mark up the attached doc and return comments by 2027-05-19 11:00 PT. If acceptable, we can route to procurement and target signature the following week.
>
> Best,
>Alex

End of thread.
